statement: Samsung's HBM4 yield has reached close to 80%, up from below 60% in early mass production in February 2026, about four months ahead of the industry's expected timeline.
why: Higher HBM4 yield converts existing wafer starts into more sellable stacks, which loosens the tightest bottleneck on advanced AI accelerator supply.

impact.mechanism: Better yield at a second qualified HBM4 supplier raises effective HBM bit supply per wafer, easing the memory constraint that gates merchant-GPU and accelerator module output.

evidence.excerpt: Samsung Electronics' HBM4 yield recently came close to the 80% mark. In the early stages of mass production in February this year, its yield struggled below 60%, but the company has since staged a dramatic turnaround.
the industry had initially expected Samsung to reach an 80% yield around the end of this year

confidence.basis: Single secondary trade-press report citing unnamed industry expectations; no filing or company disclosure corroborates the yield figure.

dispersion: conflicting same-key reports: statement/trend changed (trend rising -> rising); sources: Seoul Economic Daily (en.sedaily.com)
